question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorine.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chlorine is the element of **Group 17 **that has two isotopes of** masses 35 and 37 amu.**
 
• The average abundance of the **isotopes is 75.77%** for **35 amu** and **24.23% for 37 amu.**
 
• Chlorine has the **atomic number 17** and its chemical symbol is **Cl.**
 
• Chlorine is a pungent,** green-yellow gas at room temperature** and makes up about** 0.0018% **of the Earth's crust.
 
• It's widely known for its use in **disinfecting drinking water** as well as in** bleach and other cleaning products**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iodine:**

 
 
• Iodine is another member of **Group 17,** the **Halogens**. It has one stable isotope:** Iodine-127.**
 
• It is a shiny**, dark-grey to purple-black** nonmetal that can be seen when it is at room temperature.
 
• Iodine is essential for the production of thyroid hormones in the human body, with **deficiency leading to goitre**, an enlargement of the thyroid gland.
 
• Its** radioisotope, iodine-131**, is used in **medical treatment, particularly for thyroid conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Fluorine:**
 
 
• Fluorine is the lightest member of the** halogens** and has only one stable isotope: **Fluorine-19.**
 
• It is a **pale, yellow-green gas** at room temperature and is the** most reactive and electronegative** of all elements.
 
• The majority of fluorine is used in the manufacture of a variety of compounds, including an important class called** fluorocarbons**, that have many **industrial applications.**
 
 
 
• **Astatine:**
 
 
• Astatine is a halogen and the** heaviest **element in **Group 17.** It is a radioactive element, and all its isotopes are short-lived; the **most stable isotope, Astatine-210, has a half-life of 8.1 hours.**
 
• It is the** rarest naturally occurring element** and is typically **produced synthetically.**
 
• Not much is known about astatine due to its scarcity, but it's believed to be a heavy, volatile, and highly reactive metalloid similar to the other halogens.
